chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Statement of Allah (Exalted and Majestic): 'And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community; and they will not cease to differ, except those on whom your Lord has mercy.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'They were one community, so Allah sent the Prophets to establish the Proof against them.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah send Prophets if He could have made all people one community?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that the initial unity of humanity was not a state of inherent faith but a pre-prophetic condition; Allah sent the Prophets to establish the 'hujjah' (divine proof) against them, which inevitably led to the divergence of beliefs. This highlights the Shia theological perspective that prophetic mission is essential for distinguishing truth from falsehood and justifying human diversity in religious adherence. The verse thus serves not merely as a description of human nature but as a theological justification for the necessity of divine guidance.
